content.text: Travel-service's `getRouteByTripId` throws IllegalArgumentException with no downstream calls, which points to an application fault inside travel-service. Next, I'll check route-plan's own spans, since its self-time is high even though its callees look mostly fine.

input.query: SELECT p, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind k, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,1) avg_ms, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,1) p95, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs FROM (SELECT 'abn' p, * FROM abnormal_traces UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', * FROM normal_traces) WHERE service_name IN ('ts-route-plan-service','ts-travel-plan-service') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: Route-plan's outbound GET calls fail after about 2.6 s on average, while travel-service answers its own requests in about 11 ms. I'll join each client span to its child server span to see where that time goes.

input.query: SELECT c.service_name caller, c.span_name, c.attr_status_code cst, s.service_name callee, s.span_name callee_span, s.attr_status_code sst, count(*) n, round(avg(c.duration)/1e6,1) c_ms, round(avg(s.duration)/1e6,1) s_ms FROM abnormal_traces c LEFT JOIN abnormal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id = c.span_id AND s.trace_id = c.trace_id AND s.attr_span_kind='Server' WHERE c.attr_span_kind='Client' AND c.service_name IN ('ts-route-plan-service','ts-food-service','ts-travel-plan-service','ts-ui-dashboard') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6 ORDER BY n DESC

content.text: The callers wait about 3.7 s for a travel response that the server reports as taking about 9 ms. That gap sits between the services, so I'll check the network-level (hubble) metrics on the travel connections.

input.query: SELECT DISTINCT metric_name FROM (SELECT * FROM abnormal_metrics_sum UNION ALL SELECT * FROM normal_metrics_sum) WHERE metric_name ILIKE '%hubble%' OR metric_name ILIKE '%tcp%' OR metric_name ILIKE '%drop%' OR metric_name ILIKE '%retrans%'

content.text: No drops or retransmissions appear on the travel connections, so the network looks normal. Next I'll check travel-service's own pod and JVM metrics, since its filesystem shift is very large.

content.text: Travel-service's pod resources look close to normal, so this is not resource exhaustion. To see where the 3.7 s goes, I'll inspect one full failing trace with timestamps.
